root_idea.summary: The root centers on softness as opposed to roughness, extending to gentleness, ease, and receptivity.
root_idea.development: Its semantic development runs from tactile or material softness to gentle conduct, ease of life, yielding acceptance, and causative softening.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The inflected QAC forms are presented under the normalized Form I citation form لَانَ.
The inflected QAC form is presented under the normalized Form IV citation form أَلَانَ.
The inflected adjective is normalized to the citation form لَيِّنٌ.
The inflected noun is presented under the citation form لِينَةٌ.

senses.definition: To deal gently and mildly with others.
senses.usage_conditions: In 3:159, it describes gentle conduct toward people rather than harshness.

senses.definition: To soften and become yielding or receptive, accepting the truth after resistance.
senses.usage_conditions: In 39:23, it is used of skins and hearts becoming softened toward the remembrance of God; the construction conveys submission and acceptance after refusal or denial.

senses.definition: To make something soft, pliable, or relaxed.
senses.usage_conditions: In 34:10, the object is iron, which is made pliable. A separate medical use involving relaxation of the bowels is recorded in Classical Arabic.

senses.definition: Gentle, mild, or soft in manner.
senses.usage_conditions: In 20:44, it describes a gentle or mild manner of speech; the adjective is not restricted to a particular object class.

senses.definition: A soft or tender palm tree.
senses.usage_conditions: In 59:5, the term refers generally to a soft palm tree and is not restricted to one particular named variety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become physically soft, smooth, pliant, supple, flexible, ductile, malleable, or lax.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Physical or material use, contrasted with roughness or harshness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the bowels to become relaxed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physiological construction concerning the condition of the bowels.
Used of a person who abandons firmness or resistance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat someone gently; to soothe, coax, or wheedle him, especially with words.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive interpersonal use, including gentleness, blandishment, and verbal coaxing.
A medical use, said of a medicine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Softness, delicateness, or ease of life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression concerning comfortable or easy living.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, delicate, or easy, especially when describing life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عَيْشٌ لَيِّنٌ.
